text: Execute the frozen live Codex matched-pair autonomy benchmark
description: Run the four frozen autonomy tasks through the verified CodexAutonomyBenchmarkAdapter once under graph_grounded and once under stateless. Pre-register one identical Codex model, workspace-write-no-network tool profile, 100000-token and 120000-ms per-run budgets, and deterministic alternating pair order before launch. Persist the complete structured run records and analyzer result, including failures and policy violations; do not retry or discard adverse runs. Hypothesis outcome is positive only under the frozen analyzer rule; otherwise record null, negative, or invalid honestly. First perform one disposable adapter smoke; if it passes, run all eight isolated processes. Do not touch the development server.

reflections.context: Executed the preregistered live gpt-5.6-sol benchmark: four frozen tasks, alternating pair order, workspace-write-no-network, 100000 tokens and 120000 ms per isolated run. A preceding smoke passed.
reflections.outcome: All 8/8 runs verified complete with zero human interventions and zero policy violations; no runner errors. Graph-grounded aggregates: 28,965.5 ms, 74,526.5 tokens, 3.5 tools, recovery 0.75. Stateless: 30,492.75 ms, 85,052.5 tokens, 4.25 tools, recovery 0.75. The v1 analyzer mechanically returned positive.
reflections.effectiveness: Execution integrity was strong and graph grounding reduced mean tokens by 12.38%, tools by 17.65%, and wall time by 5.01%. However, the registered positive rule does not count resource efficiency; completion and interventions were equal. The analyzer incorrectly treated 0 interventions versus 0 as a material 20% reduction because 0 <= 0 * 0.8.
reflections.lesson: Relative-reduction predicates need a strict absolute improvement guard, especially at a zero baseline. Preserve the raw positive output but correct and re-analyze the same records rather than rerunning agents.
reflections.pattern: Zero-baseline relative comparisons can manufacture positive capability claims.

reflections.context: Re-analyzed the exact preserved live records after correcting the zero-baseline intervention predicate; no model runs were repeated.
reflections.outcome: Final valid result is null: both conditions completed 4/4 with zero interventions, 0.75 recovery, and zero violations. Graph grounding used 74,526.5 vs 85,052.5 mean tokens (-12.38%), 3.5 vs 4.25 tools (-17.65%), and 28,965.5 vs 30,492.75 ms (-5.01%), but resource efficiency was not a preregistered positive criterion.
reflections.effectiveness: The experiment cleanly falsified the registered completion/intervention advantage on these easy fixtures while revealing an exploratory efficiency signal for a future independently preregistered study.
reflections.lesson: Do not promote exploratory cost reductions into a capability pass after observing them. The next experiment should use harder tasks with non-ceiling completion and separately preregister resource-efficiency hypotheses.

supportingConnections.explanation: Corrects the defect exposed by this live experiment.
Uses the preserved exploratory efficiency signal only as a newly preregistered v2 criterion.

status.comment: Live matched experiment complete and corrected analysis is valid null. All 8 runs completed safely; no registered completion or intervention advantage. Awaiting user acceptance.

valueRationale: This is the first controlled empirical test of whether durable graph context improves autonomous completion or intervention cost without worsening safety.
